newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: New Austrian finmin fails to convince markets.
newsitem.headline: New Austrian finmin fails to convince markets.

text.p: Austrian chancellor-in-waiting Viktor Klima on Friday named Social Democrat Vienna finance chief Rudolf Edlinger as finance minister, dashing market hopes for an expert outsider rather than a career politician.
The appointment of Social Democrat Edlinger was the final piece in Klima's ministerial jigsaw and marked the end of a one-week struggle to fill the key post in his new cabinet.
President Thomas Klestil will swear in the team on Tuesday.
Analysts described Edlinger, 56, as a little-known regional politician with scant experience to prepare him for his new role in Austria's sometimes fractious coalition government.

The professional lithographer, a member of the ruling Social Democrats since 1958, will have the arduous task of steering Austria into Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), tackling tricky budget disputes along the way.

"Very little is known about him," a London-based Austria analyst told Reuters, speaking on condition of anonymity. "But in any case, he's a political heavyweight and not the kind of expert minister that the business community had hoped for."
The treasury post became vacant over the weekend when Franz Vranitzky named Klima his successor as chancellor and Social Democratic Party leader.
Financial markets failed to derive much inspiration from Edlinger's appointment, with the ATX index of 21 blue chips closing down almost 0.7 percent after the announcement.
"We're certainly not going to jump for joy," said one analyst at a Vienna bank.
Edlinger wasted no time in reassuring the public that he would give his all to his new job. "I will dedicate the necessary energy to this tough task," he said.

Klima insisted Edlinger was well-equipped to put Austria firmly on course for early EMU membership. "I think Edlinger is an excellent choice," he said after presenting his new cabinet line-up to President Klestil.

But in an apparent move to ease market worries, Klima also announced he had named Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer, deputy chief executive at Austrian oil and energy group OMV, to the newly-created post of state secretary of finance.
The 46-year old Ruttenstorfer, one of Austria's most respected business leaders, will manage preparations for EMU and oversee financial market reforms.

Edlinger has served as the City of Vienna's finance chief since November 1994 and has borne responsibility for by far Austria's biggest regional budget, with annual expenditure of around 134 billion schillings ($11.68 billion).
He was a key player in a political team that two weeks ago hammered out a coalition deal over the sale of Austria's most famous bank Creditanstalt to market leader Bank Austria.
The heavy-set smoker had insisted earlier this week that he was not a candidate to take over the finance portfolio, saying he wanted to retire by the year 2000 after three decades in local politics.

Klima's first choice for finance minister, Burgenland regional government leader Karl Stix, turned down the job on Thursday because of bickering within the regional coalition of Social Democrats and conservative People's Party. The People's Party had refused to guarantee its backing for a Social Democrat to replace Stix if he departed for Vienna.
But Klima insisted Edlinger was not a second-rate candidate: "I had a choice of two excellent candidates."
